title: bedscout
text: bedscout library wraps useful functionality around BED file annotations mostly shape GRanges objects. Currently implemented functions belong one following categories: Arithmetic: Overlap-related simple operations can performed two GRanges objects, currently: loci_overlap, bp_overlap, fc_enrichment jaccard_index, loci_consensus. Pairwise: Scoring functions compare lists GRanges pairwise --kind manner. , pairwise_score computes arbitrary score function (anything takes two GRanges objects inputs), including ones mentioned arithmetic section. returns data frame long format (triplets gr1, gr2, score) plays nice plotting libraries like ggplot2. fixed example pairwise_enrichment, exactly pairwise_score scoring function fixed fc_enrichment. Annotate: Intersect GRanges object corresponding named elements another GRanges. can gene TSS, ChromHMM segmentations anything really name field. annotations can done proximity (annotate_nearby_feature), overlap (annotate_overlapping_features), overlap maximizing jaccard index (impute_feature), especially useful genomic segmentations like ChromHMM. Venn: Venn-diagram like operations. Right now, relevant function calculate_venn_intersections calculates intersections possible subsets GRanges list. can used plot venn diagrams. Plot: handy plotting functions - plot_euler makes use eulerr package make Euler diagram overlaps list GRanges objects. plot_pairwise_score plot_combinations_score matched pairwise operations plot heatmap specified score.

what: Imputing elements from a genomic segmentation annotation
title: bedscout
text: many cases, one set genomic loci like know type genomic features overlap . impute_features takes GRanges object named list GRanges objects, one per interest feature type. One classic example annotating genomic segmentations like ChromHMM. cases, almost always case loci interest group overlaps one feature, since genomic segmentations partitions genome. impute_features takes overlap select estimated best match, one maximal jaccard_index. prevents flanking empty segments (usually tagged “quiescent”) preferred, overlap tends significantly larger. segments.bed contains example type BED file, name file must category (.e. gene annotation file locus different gene name useful process way). instance: unique loci completely contains Type_C element flanks also overlap larger Type_A loci. can ask bedscout impute overlap optimizes jaccard_index. Additionally, one can specify ties handled, unusual case locus jaccard score one loci overlaps . default, impute_features parameter with_ties equals TRUE, means ties reported comma separated list (unique features). with_ties set FALSE one features reported.
code: genome_segment_file <- system.file(   "extdata",   "segments.bed",   package = "bedscout" ) cat(readLines(genome_segment_file), sep = '\n') #> chr1 0   1000    Type_A  .   * #> chr1 1001    1100    Type_B  .   * #> chr1 1101    5000    Type_A  .   * #> chr1 5001    5020    Type_C  .   * #> chr1 5021    10000   Type_A  .   * #> chr1 10001   10100   Type_D  .   * #> chr1 10101   20000   Type_A  .   * #> chr1 20001   20005   Type_E  .   * #> chr1 20006   20060   Type_F  .   * #> chr1 20061   20160   Type_C  .   * #> chr1 20161   30000   Type_A  .   * gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(   seqnames = c("chr1"),   IRanges::IRanges(4971, 5050),   strand = "+" ) # rtracklayer can import BED files into GRanges to use with impute_feature gr_features <- rtracklayer::import(genome_segment_file) gr_imputed <- impute_feature(gr, gr_features, "name") gr_imputed #> GRanges object with 1 range and 2 metadata columns: #>       seqnames    ranges strand | impute_score  annotation #>          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> |    <numeric> <character> #>   [1]     chr1 4971-5050      + |       0.2375      Type_C #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

what: Obtaining a consensus loci set out of a list of GRanges objects
title: bedscout
text: Sometimes might want obtain genomic annotation consensus group annotations. typical example peaks called set replicates. , can use loci_consensus function, takes list GRanges objects returns single GRanges object consensus loci. parameters function min_consensus, defaults 1. means locus appears least one lists considered, equivalent merging ranges. also possible resize ranges fixed size getting consensus list: can also generate peak universe merging across replicates consensus joining loci appear conditions. type operation can used prepare differential peak analysis strategies like PCA:
code: loci_consensus(peak_grlist, min_consensus = 3) #> GRanges object with 2 ranges and 0 metadata columns: #>       seqnames    ranges strand #>          <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> #>   [1]     chr1   151-200      * #>   [2]     chr1   531-550      * #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths loci_consensus(peak_grlist, min_consensus = 2, resize = 500, anchor = "start") #> GRanges object with 6 ranges and 0 metadata columns: #>       seqnames        ranges strand #>          <Rle>     <IRanges>  <Rle> #>   [1]     chr1      151-1030      * #>   [2]     chr1     2031-2500      * #>   [3]     chr1     4001-4600      * #>   [4]     chr1   11001-11500      * #>   [5]     chr1   50301-50800      * #>   [6]     chr1 100221-100500      * #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths peaks_list <- list(   "condition_A" = peak_files[1:2],   "condition_B" = peak_files[2:3] )  peaks_universe(peaks_list, min_consensus = 2) #> GRanges object with 6 ranges and 1 metadata column: #>       seqnames      ranges strand |                 source #>          <Rle>   <IRanges>  <Rle> |            <character> #>   [1]     chr1     151-250      * | condition_A,conditio.. #>   [2]     chr1     531-555      * | condition_A,conditio.. #>   [3]     chr1   4001-4050      * |            condition_A #>   [4]     chr1   4101-4250      * |            condition_B #>   [5]     chr1 11001-11030      * |            condition_B #>   [6]     chr1 70221-70350      * |            condition_B #>   ------- #>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths
